The *Dhutaṅgapañha* ("The Voluntary Austerities") is a section of the *Milindapañha* (Mil 6.4.2) preserved in the late canonical and paracanonical Pali prose literature [SuttaCentral]. The text discusses ascetic practices (*dhutaṅga*) and is referenced in connection with the *Ekakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 1.170), the *Gotamivatthadānapañha* (Mil 6.1.2), and the Vinaya *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (*Nissaggiya Pācittiya* 15) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records three translations across three languages [SuttaCentral].
Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus indicates extensive internal sharing with the Pali corpus, identifying 702 matching passages across 75 texts [DharmaNexus]. Major alignments occur with the *Milindaṭīkā* (*Sihaḷa-gantha-saṅgaho*), adjacent *Milindapañha* chapters such as the *Bāhirakathā* (Mil 2) and *Anumānapañha* (Mil 6.4.1), and the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 1, especially §62.1 aligning with AN 1.175–187, and AN 4) [DharmaNexus]. In agreement with SuttaCentral's cross-references, DharmaNexus also identifies shared segments with the Vinaya *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (*Nissaggiya Pācittiya* 15 at §58.1–58.2, as well as *Pārājika* 4), as well as commentary works including the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā*, *Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā*, and *Buddhavaṃsa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-linguistically, DharmaNexus aligns passages of the text with several Tibetan Mahāyāna works, including the *Ārya-amitābhavyūha-nāma-mahāyāna-sūtra* (D0049), the *Mahāsūtrasamuccaya-nāma* (D3961), and the *Ārya-mañjuśrībuddhakṣetraguñavyūhanāma-mahāyānasūtra* (D0059) [DharmaNexus].
